transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I can’t seem to stay focused on what I’m doing at the machines long enough to do the job the way they need me to. Since our plant upgraded to faster, more complex lines, I've really struggled and ended up on a performance improvement plan. My union rep suggested I come in to see if there's an underlying attention issue before things get worse.

Can you tell me more about what happens when you try to focus on your work, such as whether you find your mind wandering, have trouble following instructions, or get easily distracted by your surroundings?

I start out really trying to watch the screens and checklists, but after a few minutes my mind just drifts and I'll catch myself staring at a machine, completely missing alarms or lights. Any little thing pulls me away—like a forklift beeping, someone walking past, or even my own thoughts about what to cook for dinner. Before I know it, I've completely stopped paying attention to the procedures I'm supposed to be following.
Do you often act on impulse or do things without thinking them through, such as interrupting others, blurting out answers, or engaging in risky behaviors?

Yes, I'm always acting on impulse, like cutting people off mid-sentence or reaching over to adjust a coworker's machine without asking because I think I have a faster way. This goes back to elementary school when I'd constantly blurt out answers in class, and it recently got dangerous when I stepped into a restricted area at work without waiting for a safety lockout. It feels like I just can't stop myself from acting before thinking.
Do you also experience restlessness or fidgeting when you're not actively engaged in a task, such as tapping your hands or feet, or getting up frequently when you're supposed to be sitting still?

Yes, I do this constantly—I'm always bouncing my leg, clicking my pen, or tapping on the rails. During long meetings or safety videos, I get this buzzing feeling in my body like I'm going to crawl out of my skin if I don't move. I end up popping out of my seat to pace in the back, get coffee, or throw things away, even though I've been warned about staying seated.
Can you tell me more about how these symptoms of restlessness and impulsivity affect your daily life outside of work, such as in social situations or at home?

Even on my days off, I can't just sit quietly to watch a show or read because I'm constantly getting up, playing with my phone, or talking over the TV. Socially, I talk way too much, go on and on with stories, and constantly cut people off mid-sentence before I even realize I'm doing it. It just feels like being calm and quiet is almost impossible for me, no matter where I am.
Do you find it difficult to engage in activities quietly, such as reading or doing puzzles, without feeling the need to be constantly moving or fidgeting?

Yes, it is incredibly hard for me to do quiet activities. Even on my days off, I can't just sit and read or watch a show without fiddling with my phone, talking over the TV, or getting up every few minutes. Trying to be calm and quiet honestly feels almost impossible for me.
Do you often feel overly restless or have difficulty engaging in leisure activities quietly, and has this been a persistent pattern throughout your life, not just a recent development?

Yes, it's definitely a lifelong pattern; even back in elementary school, I was always the kid getting in trouble for wandering around and not staying in my seat. Whenever I'm forced to be still, I get this intense buzzing in my body like I'm going to crawl out of my skin. It's why I've never been able to just sit quietly and read or watch a show without constantly moving or getting up.
